newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH '98 STATE SPENDING 191-192 BLN - VIRTANEN.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH '98 STATE SPENDING 191-192 BLN - VIRTANEN.

text.p: Finnish 1998 state budget expenditure will be flat over 1997 at 191-192 billion markka, according to a finance ministry proposal to the government, budget chief Erkki Virtanen said on Monday.
The government is scheduled to decide on Tuesday on the budget spending frames for 1998 and 1999.

"This will be the most routine, the easiest of any round of budget frame talks for this government so far," Virtanen said by telephone. "In a broad fiscal policy perspective there are no problems in sight," he said.

In 1998, budget spending would be 191-192 billion markka, Virtanen said. "Adjusted for inflation, spending will be flat compared to this year, he said, referring to the 1997 state budget expenditure total of 190.31 billion markka.
The outlook for 1999 was similar, Virtanen said, but he declined to give any detailed figures.

"The fiscal policy target is that state indebtedness will be brought under control and this will happen if taxes remain relatively high, the projected growth materialises, we stand by already made spending cuts and we implement other decisions already made," he said, but did not elaborate.
The deficit of the state finances would fall to about 20 billion markka in 1998 and slightly further in 1999 from some 28 billion markka forecast by the ministry this year, he said.
The five-party left-right-green government's budget frame talks are due to start on Tuesday at 0930/0730 GMT and a news conference is scheduled around midday, the government said in a statement.
